gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's enclosure-only prices side by side from the maker stores: ACASIS TB501Pro (Gen5 firmware) $174, TB501 Max $179, TB504mini fanless $179, basic TB501Pro $149, OWC Express 1M2 80G 0TB $199.99, Satechi DotDisk $199.99, ORICO X50 $199.99, so the cheapest Gen5-capable fan-cooled JHL9480 box undercuts every fanless rival by about $26.
standout_why: The three cited pages have no cross-brand prices at all: the two acasis.com product pages price only ACASIS ($149 basic, $174 Pro), DPReview's roundup names no prices and tests one TB5 drive (OWC Envoy Ultra), and OWC's blog names only OWC products with no prices. The uncited picklog.cc result (rank 4) does hold a 14-model price table, but it is dated 2026-09-11 and already stale: it lists OWC Express 1M2 80G at $149.99, while OWC's own store shows $199.99 today. Macworld (rank 6) prices only complete drives and lists OWC at $219.99. No page combines today's prices with the one reason each model loses.
decides: Confirms ChatGPT's value pick but sharpens it: for a MacBook Pro M4 Pro/Max with a Samsung 990 Pro inside, the $174 ACASIS TB501Pro (Gen5-capable firmware, manual fan) is the cheapest full-feature TB5 enclosure today; the $149 basic TB501Pro saves $25 only if you never move to a PCIe 5.0 SSD. The OWC Express 1M2 80G at $199.99 is no longer the $149.99 bargain picklog listed; it now costs the same as Satechi's DotDisk and ORICO's X50, so you pay $26 over ACASIS purely for fanless silence and OWC's 2-year warranty. For a base-M4 MacBook Pro (Thunderbolt 4 only) none of these beat a $54.90 ACASIS 40Gbps enclosure, since the host caps the link at 40Gbps.

findings.label: Price, enclosure only, ACASIS US store
findings.source_title: Acasis 80Gbps M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure Compatible with Thunderbolt 5
findings.note: Shopify catalogue read via storecheck search; page states Intel JHL9480(B2), native PCIe Gen5 support, manual fan button with auto-start at 55 °C, no PD charging. Loses only on noise versus fanless rivals; SSDs with heatsinks do not fit.

findings.label: Price, enclosure only, ACASIS US store
findings.source_title: Acasis 80Gbps M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure with Temp-Control Fan & PD Port
findings.note: Same JHL9480 board as TB501Pro but automatic fan (starts at 55 °C, no manual button) plus a PD port for 60 W laptop charging. Loses on $5 extra and no manual fan control.

findings.label: Price, enclosure only, ACASIS US store
findings.source_title: Acasis 80Gbps M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure with Fanless Cooling
findings.note: Fanless deep-fin design, JHL9480 + RTL9210 fallback, optional PD port, PCIe Gen5 up to 8 TB. ACASIS claims up to 6,831 MB/s write and 6,168 MB/s read (maker figure, no host named). Loses to OWC on warranty disclosure (none stated) and to TB501Pro on price by $5.

findings.label: Price, enclosure only, ACASIS US store
findings.source_title: Acasis 80Gbps M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure (Gen 5 SSD Not Supported)
findings.note: Page states this is firmware 56.56 and is not compatible with PCIe Gen 5 SSDs. Cheapest TB5 enclosure found today; loses on Gen5 support only, which does not matter with a Samsung 990 Pro.

findings.label: Price, 0TB DIY enclosure, OWC store
findings.note: Capacities: 1TB $489.00, 2TB $749.99, 4TB $1,349.99, 8TB $2,429.99. 2-year OWC limited warranty. Fanless deep-finned aluminium. Claims over 6,000 MB/s on TB5/USB4 80G hosts (AJA System Test, 2 TB drive, Mac Studio M3 Ultra), over 3,800 on 40G USB4, up to 2,800 on TB3 Mac. Cable length not stated. Loses on price: $26 more than ACASIS TB501Pro, and $50 above the $149.99 picklog.cc recorded on 2026-09-11.

findings.label: Price, enclosure only, Satechi store
findings.note: Store listing describes precision-milled aluminium with smart active cooling, 'one of the smallest active-cooled storage solutions'. Loses on price parity with OWC while having a fan, and the earlier-sourced 30 cm cable (9to5Toys, May 2026) is the shortest in the group.

findings.label: Price, enclosure only, ORICO US store
findings.source_title: ORICO X50 80Gbps Thunderbolt 5 Compatible Portable SSD/M.2 Enclosure
findings.note: Fanless 4-layer passive design, 0 dB. FAQ states speed is limited to 40Gbps on TB4/USB4 hosts. Loses on price: same $199.99 as OWC without OWC's stated 2-year warranty; the $579.99 compare-at is not a credible former price.

findings.label: Amazon US price, comparison only (not for the page)
findings.source_title: ORICO 80Gbps M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure PCIE 5.0 Silent Fanless ... X50PRO
findings.note: amzcheck ASIN read: 2,224 ratings, 66% five-star. Not found as a separate SKU on oricotechs.com. Notebookcheck (read 2026-11-08) measured about 6,000 MB/s read and about 3,000 MB/s write on a MacBook Pro 16 M5 over TB5 and lists the X50PRO at $329–330 with a 1 TB SSD; it states PCIe 5 SSDs are not supported, contradicting the Amazon title. Loses on the lowest measured TB5 write speed of the group and the highest enclosure-only price found.

findings.note: 5-year OWC limited warranty. Footnote states sustained writes drop to about 1,350 MB/s (2TB) and 1,700 MB/s (4TB) after the initial burst. This is the drive DPReview tested, not an enclosure; loses on price versus a $174 enclosure plus a 2 TB 990 Pro.

findings.note: Sabrent store states 'transfers up to 64Gbps', i.e. the PCIe 4.0 x4 ceiling. No Sabrent TB5 bare enclosure appears in the store search; its only 80Gbps-class product is this sealed drive. Loses on being non-upgradable at roughly 2.5 times the enclosure-plus-SSD cost.

findings.label: Price, TB4/USB4 enclosure for base-M4 MacBook Pro, ACASIS US store
findings.source_title: Acasis 40Gbps M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure Compatible with Thunderbolt 4/3
findings.note: Intel JHL7440, TB5/4/3 and USB4 only, no USB 3.x fallback. The base M4 MacBook Pro is Thunderbolt 4 only, so a TB5 enclosure gains nothing on it; this is the price floor for the same 40Gbps result.
